source.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons
source.authors: C. NancyBaygorrea; Martins Gomes Otávio da Fonseca

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly evaluates label-noise fitting on an MLP, but distinguishes complementary-label corruption from uniformly random labels and reports incomplete fitting under its main protocol. It also tests convergence and corrupted-label memorization across optimizer variants.
record.gate_note: The introduction cites prior evidence for fitting randomly assigned labels; that citation is not this study's result. Its own results concern synthetic noise and do not test shuffled pixels or Gaussian inputs. Reported aggregate values are retained as the paper presents them; figures without textual results are not extracted as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: Own experiments measure random-label fitting, corruption-rate effects and early learning before memorization. Results qualify fitting claims by optimizer and training horizon; complementary-label corruption must be distinguished from fully random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the fitting and noise-mechanism conclusions but omits the paper's main measurement conclusions. The information term tracks memorization closely and adds mainly a zero population null, much of whose practical advantage chance correction recovers. Statistical complexity precedes memorization at low UI noise and coincides with it at high noise, where confidence effects cannot be separated; it performs poorly against established stopping and detection tools. Fitting is incomplete under constant-rate Adam but interpolation occurs with SGD and some cosine schedules. Conclusions remain limited to one MLP, two small datasets and synthetic noise.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a single 784-512-512-10 MLP with Adam and synthetic class-conditional label-noise mechanisms; the main experiment does not reproduce the original random-label intervention, and reports extensions with SGD and cosine scheduling.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with the corruption mechanism (UI, SU, PERM, pair-flip), corruption rate, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and weight decay. Under UI, interpolation depends on training variant; fully corrupted UI retains true-class information unlike SU and PERM.

fits_no_version.finding: Statistical complexity remains able to distinguish noisy from clean runs after interpolation, with AUROC 0.97–1.00 under several matching procedures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Predictive complexity can retain differences between clean-label and noisy-label training after interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay produces softer predictions and a signal-term deviation of 0.032 at ρ=0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight decay changes predictive softness under partial UI noise.

record.problems: Only one MLP architecture and two small image datasets; synthetic class-conditional noise only. Main protocol did not interpolate corrupted runs; extension analyses are exploratory. Ten seeds per condition, bootstrap intervals may undercover, and some comparisons are descriptive or have stated limitations. The study does not test the original random-label intervention or unstructured inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 6 contains a flattened section in which some accuracy-column assignments are not safely reconstructable; those values are not assigned beyond what the text makes clear.

untested.parts: Eventual fitting beyond 200 epochs for SU/PERM and replication across architectures. UI optimizer extensions do not establish eventual fitting of independent random labels.
Matched convergence times for fully independent random labels and a clear monotonic convergence-time trend across corruption rates. SGD supplies an epoch ratio, not a measured wall-clock ratio.
All shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel and Gaussian-input conditions.
A full corruption-rate sweep using SU or PERM. Optimizer extensions do not provide complete numerical test-error trajectories in the text.
Whether weight decay, dropout or augmentation prevent fitting completely random labels; matched removal experiments on true-label generalization.
Generality beyond this MLP and synthetic noise; separate fully random versus true-label training dynamics are not directly compared for early semantic learning.

missing.what: Matched SGD convergence baseline: clean runs interpolate at median epoch 18, noisy runs at 113–122. Add to R4; the V2 verdict uses this text.
Fashion-MNIST UI: no corrupted run interpolates, M reaches 0.9 in only one of ten runs at ρ=0.8, and full UI corruption yields 1.6% test accuracy.
Pair-flip fitting results: interpolation fraction 0.03 on MNIST and 0.00 on Fashion-MNIST. Record separately from uniform noise because pair-flip has structured class transitions.
Noise-rate-dependent memorization timing: UI t50 rises from 18.2 to 23.2 epochs over ρ=0.2–0.8; hard-information t50 rises from 19.9 to 34.0. These are intermediate thresholds, not convergence times.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Failure to reach 99.9% accuracy alone does not refute V1, which allows near-zero error; the substantially incomplete SU/PERM fitting warrants a horizon-specific scope limit. UI labels remain dependent on the true class even at full corruption. The source's flattened Table 6 is reconstructable from its column vectors and adjoining prose; several extracted values were assigned to the wrong measures.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test completely random labels in the original study's settings or test error at chance under uniform random labels; tests several synthetic corruption mechanisms with one MLP and modified training variants.
Does not measure the small-constant-factor training-time comparison against true-label training. Reports interpolation epochs for some noisy-label training variants.

Does not test uniform random relabeling through a full corruption-rate sweep; its UI noise always assigns an incorrect class, while SU and PERM are evaluated only at full corruption. Does not establish a general steadily rising test-error curve through all corruption fractions.
Tests absence of weight decay and a weight-decay variant, but does not test dropout or data augmentation, nor whether removing regularization alone worsens true-label generalization.
Measures clean-label retention and noisy-label fitting over epochs under UI noise; does not compare completely random labels against true labels as separate training runs.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam at constant learning rate on UI-noisy MNIST labels for 200 epochs; reports final training accuracy, test accuracy, and memorized fraction.
rows.measure: Final training accuracy against noisy labels; best and final test accuracy against clean labels; final memorized fraction M against noisy labels.
rows.baseline: For ρ = 0, final training accuracy 0.986 (0.001), best test accuracy 0.985 (0.001), final test accuracy 0.973 (0.001); clean-label comparison at same model and protocol.
rows.value: For ρ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8: final train accuracy 0.973 (0.001), 0.965 (0.002), 0.948 (0.002), 0.863 (0.007); best test accuracy 0.855 (0.005), 0.659 (0.011), 0.430 (0.009), 0.200 (0.006); final test accuracy 0.986 (0.001), 0.965 (0.002), 0.948 (0.002), 0.863 (0.007) as displayed in Table 6. For ρ = 1, final training accuracy not reported, test accuracy 0.5% [0.5, 0.6] in Section 5.6, and final M = 0.962.
rows.uncertainty: Table 6 reports standard deviation in parentheses; the ρ = 1 test accuracy is 0.5% [0.5, 0.6].
rows.note: The supplied Table 6 flattened layout makes the last two accuracy columns hard to assign reliably; the values in those columns are transcribed only where their mapping is clear from the column headings and adjoining prose. Section 5.6 separately states final ρ=1 test accuracy. At ρ=1, UI assigns incorrect complementary labels, not uniformly random labels; training did not reach interpolation for any corrupted run under the main protocol.
rows.check: Table 6 columns are misassigned. For ρ=0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1, final training accuracy is 1.000,0.992,0.987,0.979,0.963,0.962. Best test accuracy is 0.986,0.973,0.965,0.948,0.863,unreported; final test accuracy is 0.985,0.855,0.659,0.430,0.200,0.005. Final M is undefined at ρ=0 and otherwise 0.979,0.980,0.974,0.962,0.962. Correct associated standard deviations using the corresponding vectors in Table 6. UI is not completely random labeling; final values alone do not establish V6. Split the combined measures into separate rows.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured final training accuracy against noisy labels and test accuracy against clean labels under fully corrupted symmetric-uniform labels.
rows.measure: Test accuracy against clean labels; normalized signal information ιsig about true class in test predictions; fraction of training labels memorized at epoch 200.
rows.baseline: Chance test accuracy is 10%; comparison is PERM and UI at ρ = 1.
rows.value: Test accuracy 10.1%; ιsig = 0.002; 86% of training labels memorized at epoch 200.
rows.note: SU generates labels uniformly over all classes, which may coincide with the clean class; this is the study's closest test of random labels. Training-label memorization is incomplete at epoch 200.
rows.check: The reported 86% is M, defined over samples whose observed label differs from the clean label; do not silently equate it with overall training accuracy. The text loosely describes training-label memorization. Chance test accuracy is established, but near-zero training error is not. Final-only measurements do not establish V6 or a corruption-rate trajectory.

source_check.correct: SU at rho=1: clean-label test accuracy 10.1%, normalized signal information 0.002, and M=0.86 at epoch 200. M is the fraction of changed-label samples predicted with their noisy label, not overall training accuracy.
source_check.problem: The 86% value has the changed-label subset as its denominator; describing it as a fraction of all training labels is inaccurate.

rows.measure: Median epoch at which training accuracy against noisy labels reached 99.9%.
rows.baseline: Main protocol Adam at constant learning rate did not interpolate in any corrupted run within 200 epochs.
rows.value: SGD reached interpolation in all its runs; median epoch 113-122 for ρ > 0.
rows.note: The stated result shows interpolation eventually occurred with SGD, but the paper does not give matched true-label training times or the time ratio requested by V2.
rows.check: The text supplies the missing matched clean-label baseline: median interpolation epoch 18 for clean SGD runs versus 113–122 for noisy runs. This is about 6.3–6.8 times as many epochs. SGD was evaluated at six rates total, including zero, hence five positive rates. All runs interpolated. UI fitting bears on V4, not the completely random-label intervention in V1.

source_check.correct: SGD was tested at six rates: rho=0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1. Five rates were nonzero. All SGD runs interpolated; median interpolation epochs were 18 for clean runs and 113–122 for noisy runs, approximately 6.3–6.8 times the clean epoch count.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained under UI noise with cosine learning-rate schedule and measured interpolation.
rows.measure: Whether training reached 99.9% accuracy against noisy labels.
rows.baseline: Main protocol Adam at constant learning rate did not interpolate in corrupted runs within 200 epochs.
rows.value: Cosine schedule reached interpolation at ρ ≤ 0.6.
rows.note: The paper does not report a time factor versus true-label training.
rows.check: The tested cosine-schedule rates were 0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8; interpolation occurred at the first three. This records successful fitting at those rates, not a training-time ratio or slowdown trend for V2. Table 13 reports an aggregate interpolation fraction of 0.75.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Extended Adam training to 400 epochs under UI noise and measured final memorization fraction and memorization information.
rows.measure: Final memorized fraction M and soft memorization term.
rows.baseline: At epoch 200, M was 0.963 at ρ=0.8 and 0.962 at ρ=1; soft memorization term 0.846 and 0.821, respectively.
rows.value: At epoch 400, M reached 0.975 and 0.978; soft memorization term reached 0.893 and 0.874; neither condition interpolated.
rows.note: At these tested high-noise rates, extending training improved fitting but did not reach interpolation.
rows.check: Substantial but incomplete fitting is partial, not absent. The measures do not establish a time ratio against clean-label convergence for V2. UI at full corruption is complementary labeling, so this cannot challenge V1's completely random-label result.

source_check.correct: At epoch 200, M=0.962 at both rho=0.8 and rho=1; 0.963 is overall training accuracy at rho=0.8. At epoch 400, M=0.975 and 0.978, and the soft memorization term is 0.893 and 0.874, versus 0.846 and 0.821 at epoch 200.
source_check.problem: The rho=0.8 baseline confuses overall training accuracy with M.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Tracked retained clean-label predictions R and memorized noisy-label predictions M at epoch 5 under UI noise.
rows.measure: Fraction of corrupted samples predicted with clean label R and noisy label M.
rows.baseline: At epoch 5, noisy-label training accuracy remained close to 1 − ρ.
rows.note: At the same epoch the network predicted the clean label for most corrupted samples, before later memorization.
rows.check: Early clean-label retention directly bears on V6. This single early epoch does not measure V4's final interpolation and test-error trajectory.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured memorized fraction M over training under UI label corruption.
rows.measure: Memorization onset, halfway time, final M; test accuracy peak and final training interpolation status.
rows.baseline: At ρ = 0, final training accuracy 0.986 (0.001), best test accuracy 0.985 (0.001).
rows.value: M onset around epochs 10–12; halfway point around epochs 18–23; final M ranged from 0.96 to 0.98; test accuracy peaked at epochs 3–6 before onset and subsequently declined; no corrupted run reached 99.9% training accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Table 6 reports mean and standard deviation over 10 seeds; timing summary ranges stated in text.
rows.note: The training set was not fit perfectly under the main protocol, and the study's UI corruption is incorrect-class noise, not independent random labeling.
rows.check: The temporal ordering fully exhibits V6: clean-label performance peaks before noisy-label memorization rises. For V4, fitting is partial because interpolation fails; split the row to assign different states. Its clean baseline is misassigned: final clean training accuracy is 1.000 and best clean test accuracy is 0.986.

source_check.correct: Clean baseline: final training accuracy 1.000, best test accuracy 0.986 (0.001), final test accuracy 0.985 (0.001). State is observed for V6 and partial for V4: early clean-label performance precedes noisy-label memorization, but corrupted runs do not interpolate under the main protocol.
source_check.problem: The clean baseline misassigns best test accuracy to training accuracy; one observed state cannot represent both V6 and the incomplete V4 fitting result.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compared fully corrupted UI, SU, and PERM noise at epoch 200.
rows.measure: Final memorized fraction M; test accuracy against clean labels; test prediction information about true class.
rows.baseline: SU and PERM: 10.1% test accuracy and ιsig = 0.002.
rows.uncertainty: UI test accuracy and ιsig are reported with intervals; no uncertainty stated for M, SU or PERM.
rows.note: At complete UI corruption, test accuracy is below chance but predictions retain information about true class. SU and PERM are at chance; the mechanisms are not interchangeable.
rows.check: Split by mechanism: SU/PERM bear on V1's random-label endpoint; UI bears on V4's dependence on the corruption mechanism. UI's below-chance accuracy is not a counterexample to independent random labeling. This largely duplicates R1–R3.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained with no dropout or weight decay under the main protocol on clean and UI-corrupted labels.
rows.measure: Final training accuracy against noisy labels and test accuracy against clean labels.
rows.baseline: Clean-label condition ρ = 0: final training accuracy 0.986 (0.001); best test accuracy 0.985 (0.001).
rows.value: Under corrupted labels, final training accuracy ranged from 0.863 to 0.973 for ρ=0.2–0.8; no corrupted run interpolated under this protocol.
rows.uncertainty: Table 6 reports standard deviations in parentheses.
rows.note: This tests training without weight decay and dropout; the study does not compare their removal against otherwise matched runs for true-label generalization.
rows.check: The clean condition supports the generalization-without-explicit-regularization component: final training accuracy 1.000, best test accuracy 0.986 and final test accuracy 0.985. The extracted corrupted training accuracies are actually best test accuracies; corrected final training accuracies are 0.992,0.987,0.979,0.963. Lack of interpolation without regularization does not show that regularization prevents fitting. No matched removal comparison establishes a causal effect of removal.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Added weight decay 10−4 under UI noise and compared with the main protocol.
rows.measure: Training interpolation status and final signal term relative to complete-memorization reference.
rows.baseline: Main protocol Adam without weight decay.
rows.value: Interpolation fraction 0.03 in Table 13; final signal term deviation from reference was 0.032 at ρ=0.2, where predictions remained softer.
rows.note: Weight decay does not prevent all noisy-label memorization; only a small proportion of the tested runs interpolated according to Table 13. The paper does not report a direct V5 test of generalization after removing regularization.
rows.check: Weight-decay runs used partial UI corruption, not completely random labels, so they do not establish V5's random-label regularization claim. The 0.03 interpolation fraction is rounded and pooled across rates. Signal-term deviation measures predictive softness, not the fraction of labels fitted.
